Subject: Atlas Health renewal — capacity expansion planning (draft)

Team,

Atlas Health (DH-5781) is moving to amend their upcoming renewal to add dedicated capacity: +8 A100 GPUs (reserved pool) and a preference for logical tenant separation. They asked for throughput guarantees (target: 95th percentile token latency and per-second throughput floor) and a single monthly committed spend increase.

Goals for this thread:
- Confirm isolation mode: logical reserved pool with tenant fencing vs. physical tenant separation.
- Validate throughput SLO phrasing we can commit to (I drafted a conservative SLO below).
- Prepare amendment language and billing/proration approach for procurement.

Draft SLO suggestion (for negotiation):
- 99.9% of inference requests served within targeted per-token latency for provisioned throughput up to the committed tokens/sec baseline.

Attachments: prelim-sizing-notes.txt (capacity assumptions), draft amendment checklist.

Next steps: Karthik — can you validate the runbook items for tenant fencing (KV cache, namespace isolation, metrics segregation)? Marissa — can you draft the amendment + billing delta for procurement and confirm accounting impact of mid-term add-on?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks — we're aligned on the high level and ready to proceed to a formal amendment. A few clarifications we need before procurement will sign: 

1) Isolation: we need confirmation that our tenant's KV cache and prefix cache will be logically fenced so that other tenants cannot read/evict our cached entries. Physical separation not required as long as encryption and logical namespaces are enforced.
2) Metrics & logs: our telemetry must be ingested into a separate metrics namespace (no shared dashboards by default).
3) Implementation window: we prefer the capacity to be available by July 12, 2027. Please advise lead time.
4) Billing: procurement needs a clear proration policy if we add capacity mid-billing-cycle.

Happy to hop on a short call this week if helpful.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Health renewal — capacity expansion planning (draft)

Hi Emma — copying the team so we have a shared record. Short answers up front, followed by implementation notes.

Yes — logical tenant fencing will meet your requirement. Specifics:
- KV/prefix cache: each customer gets a namespaced cache keyspace. Eviction and cache management are scoped per-namespace; other tenants cannot access or evict Atlas keys.
- Metrics & logs: we will configure a dedicated metrics namespace and a separate ingestion pipeline to your account's telemetry. Dashboards are not shared by default.
- GPU affinity & reserved pool: we will allocate an 8-GPU reserved pool (A100 equivalent) with node pinning to ensure capacity locality. The pool is logically isolated (scheduling keyspace) and will not be used for burst capacity from other tenants.
- Throughput SLO: we can commit to a throughput floor (tokens/sec baseline) and a latency objective. For the amendment, suggested phrasing: "Redwood will make available the committed reserved pool capacity and use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that 99.0% of inference requests are served within the agreed latency profile when traffic is within the committed throughput baseline." We keep a conservative wording to avoid hard legal SLA exposure.

Implementation notes (high level):
1) Provision reserved pool + node affinity: 10 business days after signed amendment.
2) Tenant fencing config (namespaces, KMS scoping): 5 business days following pool provisioning.
3) Telemetry pipeline separation: parallel configuration, 3 business days to cutover with validation.
4) Canary: we recommend a 48-72 hour canary where 10% of traffic is served from the new pool before full routing.

Attachments: isolation-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook steps), capacity-specs.xlsx (GPU topology and perf numbers).

Let me know if that timeline meets your July 12 target. If we get a signed amendment by May 10, we can hit July 12 with the recommended canary window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
